name: The Bolshoi
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Two Wiltshire punks moved to London, turned their dark streak into pop songs, toured from Poland to South America, and left a fourth album sitting on reference cassettes for 27 years.

eras.title: Trevor Flynn plays bass in Moskow
eras.text: Before the Bolshoi, Trevor Tanner and drummer Jan Kalicki were a Trowbridge rhythm section in a punk band called Moskow. The single they cut kept getting reissued for years after the band was gone.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Moskow · World of The Bolshoi: Discography
years.h: Moskow cuts "Man From U.N.C.L.E." with Tanner on bass
years.p: Tanner plays under his mother's maiden name, Trevor Flynn; Kalicki drums. Manager Allan Partner later starts TW Records, and the single comes out again in 1979 and 1982.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Bolshoi · Beggars Banquet: The Bolshoi
years.h: Tanner and Kalicki start the Bolshoi with Graham Cox on bass
years.p: Tanner sings and plays guitar now. Wikipedia places the start in Trowbridge in 1984; Beggars says London, 1983.

eras.title: Spiky mullets on Situation Two
eras.text: The band moved to London and played clubs until the papers noticed. Situation Two, the Beggars Banquet sister label, put out the first records, and Beggars signed them that summer.

years.cap: The Bolshoi on stage in London, c. 1985
years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Discography · The Quietus: The Bolshoi, The Arkive · World of The Bolshoi: I.R.S. Records bio, March 1986
years.h: "Sob Story" lands on Situation Two
years.p: SIT 38, backed with "Ports of Amsterdam." The Quietus hears dark, tribal post-punk, with Jacques Brel and Jimi Hendrix covers on the flip.

years.cap: The Bolshoi in a Beggars Banquet press photo, c. 1985
years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Beggars Banquet UK bio, October 1986 · Wikipedia: The Bolshoi
years.h: Beggars Banquet signs the band; Nick Chown takes the bass
years.p: The Beggars UK bio dates the deal to summer 1985. [[Nick Chown|6bbdaa1d-07d9-4e59-9046-1fa178104937]] replaces Graham Cox the same year.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: I.R.S. Records bio, March 1986 · Wikipedia: The Bolshoi · World of The Bolshoi: Discography
years.h: Radio One plays "Happy Boy"
years.p: Simon Boswell remixes it for the single, BBC Radio One picks it up, and it reaches No. 29 on the UK indie chart.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: I.R.S. Records bio, March 1986 · World of The Bolshoi: Discography · The Quietus: The Bolshoi, The Arkive
years.h: Giants, six songs produced with Laurence Burridge
years.p: The mini-album, SITUM 15. The Quietus says Tanner's sardonic, half-spoken baritone runs the whole record.
years.xp:
Six tracks: "Fly," "Sliding Seagulls," "Hail Mary," "Giants," "Happy Boy" and "By the River." The band co-produced with Laurence Burridge.

I.R.S. Records released it in America in 1986, and in 1990 Beggars expanded it on CD as Bigger Giants.

years.big: "Before this man had a following he must have incited riots"
q: Before this man had a following he must have incited riots
years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Beggars Banquet UK bio, October 1986 · World of The Bolshoi: I.R.S. Records bio, March 1986
years.h: Melody Maker sizes up Tanner on a London stage
years.p: Melody Maker's verdict, quoted in both label bios. By 1986 the band headlines packed nights at the Marquee.

eras.title: Keyboards, America and Peter Murphy
eras.text: Paul Clark's keyboards pulled the songs toward pop, Mick Glossop produced, and I.R.S. took the band to America. This was the year the Bolshoi went furthest from Trowbridge: the US, South America, Poland.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Discography · World of The Bolshoi: Beggars Banquet UK bio, October 1986 · World of The Bolshoi: Beggars/RCA bio, August 1987 · Wikipedia: The Bolshoi
years.h: "Away" goes to No. 1 on the American college chart
years.p: Mick Glossop produces the first Beggars single, with Leeds keyboardist [[Paul Clark|e82dc152-4ff8-4ee0-b74c-c76b1cad862a]] now in the band. In the UK it stalls at No. 100; the RCA bio says it topped the CMJ chart.

years.cap: The Bolshoi, Beggars Banquet press photo, c. 1986
years.src: World of The Bolshoi: I.R.S. Records bio, March 1986 · Wikipedia: The Bolshoi · C86 Show: The Bolshoi Brothers
years.h: I.R.S. signs them for America, and the touring starts
years.p: The March 1986 I.R.S. bio plans a first US visit for May, aiming at "worldwide domination by the end of 1986." That year takes them across the US, South America and Poland.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Discography · World of The Bolshoi: Beggars Banquet UK bio, October 1986
years.h: Reading Festival, the same month as "Books on the Bonfire"
years.p: The single comes out August 18, with a bonus 12-inch called Give It Some Vol. 1. The Beggars bio lists a 1986 Reading Festival slot.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Beggars Banquet UK bio, October 1986 · Beggars Banquet: The Bolshoi · The Quietus: The Bolshoi, The Arkive · Wikipedia: The Bolshoi
years.h: Friends, ten songs and a lot more keyboard
years.p: Produced by Mick Glossop, out on Beggars and I.R.S. The Quietus calls it a more accessible, commercial record than Giants.
years.xp:
Beggars' own bio describes the songs as suburban surrealism: lyrics drawn from people on the margins, with boredom, inadequacy and violence underneath, rather than love songs.

Critics kept calling them goth. Beggars says they flirted with it, and the closest comparison in the press was their labelmates [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]].

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Beggars Banquet UK bio, October 1986 · World of The Bolshoi: Beggars/RCA bio, August 1987
years.h: Opening for Peter Murphy on his UK tour
years.p: The band supports former Bauhaus singer [[Peter Murphy|b78346af-e3ce-4b36-a0d5-032414de8a27]] and later opens for [[Love and Rockets|8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430]] too.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Discography · Music Authentic: The Bolshoi Brothers
years.h: "Sunday Morning" becomes the song people find later
years.p: A single from Friends. Beggars' upload of the video has passed 13 million views.

eras.title: Lindy's Party, then the album that stayed on tape
eras.text: Lindy's Party went further into pop, RCA took it in America, and the reviews were warm. A fourth album was recorded, and then the band was over.

years.src: World of The Bolshoi: Beggars/RCA bio, August 1987
years.h: Tanner introduces himself as Eric Clapton
years.p: The 1987 RCA bio tells it: at one show Tanner announced "the most talented guitarist in all of Christendom: Eric Clapton."

years.h: "Sunday Morning" on Argentine TV's Badía & Cía
years.p: A fan upload shows the band on the Buenos Aires variety show in 1987, the South American leg of their travels.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Bolshoi · World of The Bolshoi: Beggars/RCA bio, August 1987 · The Quietus: The Bolshoi, The Arkive · World of The Bolshoi: Discography
years.h: Lindy's Party goes for the pop charts
years.p: BEGA 86, with RCA in the US, after the singles "Please" and "T.V. Man." Underground called it "dangerously catchy."
years.xp:
TC Wall in Underground: "completely confident, commercial, professional," and a record that would be "caressed for generations."

The Gavin Report heard "an odd cross between the Sisters of Mercy and the Dream Academy." The Quietus, years later, called it even more commercial than Friends: pop-funk and keyboard-driven moodiness.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Bolshoi · Beggars Banquet: The Bolshoi · Beggars Banquet: The Bolshoi 5 CD box · The Quietus: The Bolshoi, The Arkive
years.h: The Bolshoi split with a fourth album in the can
years.p: Wikipedia blames trouble with the label's management over recording; Beggars' own bio says internal issues. Country Life goes unreleased.
years.xp:
The songs survived mostly as demos on reference cassettes. Beggars dates the album to around 1988; The Quietus to 1989.

Tanner later moved to the US and fronted the Celtic rock band Rathkeltair and the folk group Gypsies Ginger. Clark also moved to America and built a solo electronic career.

eras.title: Country Life, rescued from cassette
eras.text: Beggars kept the catalog in print, and in 2015 the lost album finally came out. Tanner and Clark, now on opposite sides of the US, started writing together again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trevor Tanner · World of The Bolshoi: Discography
years.h: Tanner puts 41 songs in a three-CD box
years.p: Bullish, Bellyache & Belch on Emperor Penguin, the first of his solo records; Eaten by the Sea follows in 2008.

years.src: Beggars Banquet: The Bolshoi 5 CD box · The Quietus: The Bolshoi, The Arkive · Wikipedia: Trevor Tanner
years.h: Country Life finally comes out, in a five-CD box
years.p: Fifteen tracks restored from reference cassettes, plus 34 unreleased recordings across the set. The Quietus says the best of it earns them more recognition.
years.xp:
The box, BBQ 2113, gives each record its own disc: Giants, Friends, Lindy's Party, Country Life, and a fifth disc of 1986 recordings called Voyage of Peculiarities.

Ben Graham's Quietus review is no puff piece: he finds Country Life uneven, but argues at least half the box deserves a far bigger audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Bolshoi
years.h: Tanner and Clark announce the Bolshoi Brothers
years.p: The news comes through the Bolshoi's official Facebook page. Their first track, "Steam Funk," arrives in November 2022.

years.src: Beggars Banquet: Country Life reissue 2024
years.h: Country Life on orange and green vinyl
years.p: Beggars presses the lost album as a double LP, BBQ 2545, with a new acoustic version of one song recorded by Tanner for it.

years.cap: Trevor Tanner and Paul Clark as the Bolshoi Brothers, 2025
years.src: Music Authentic: The Bolshoi Brothers · C86 Show: The Bolshoi Brothers
years.h: The Bolshoi Brothers album, made between Florida and Seattle
years.p: Tanner and Clark recorded it remotely during lockdown; Clark mixed it. Eleven songs on Electronic Music Records, with live dates planned to mix in Bolshoi songs.
